newsitem.title: USA: Postponing Haiti vote "rational step", U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: Postponing Haiti vote "rational step", U.S. says.

text.p: The United States said on Friday that postponing second-round balloting in Haiti's Senate elections was a "rational step", provided a firm date was fixed to hold them.
Election officals announced on Thursday that the vote set for Sunday would be postponed indefinitely. The move came three days after the resignation of Prime Minister Rosny Smarth.
Most of the major parties had already announced they would boycott the ballot.
"We certainly think that a postponement for the sake of strengthening the electoral process is a rational step," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
"This will allow sufficient time for the (electoral) council to implement measures which will enhance the integrity and transparency of the electoral process," Burns told a news briefing.

"We hope that this postponement will promote fairness. And we also hope, in contrast to the last Haitian election, where there was a very low turnout, that postponing it may allow the Haitian authorities to make sure that the broadest number of people participate."
"We think this probably on balance makes sense to postpone, with the understanding that these elections will be held with a date certain to be provided by the Haitian government," Burns added.
